anchor_definition: The anchor is the GET request wrapper A: its body generates rast = (new Date).getTime() and appends &rast=/?rast= to the URL before issuing the GET. The rast value is a bare timestamp generated inline (no helper, no crypto), so there is no nested target-specific (0.7) or core-utility (0.5) function below A to award. On the observed request path above A is the loginmobile request function i (e="/sso/loginmobile"; A(e,t)) — a Path/Wrapper (0.2). Off-chain (0): the sibling /sso API functions o (login), s (loginmobilePwd), c (logout) that route OTHER endpoints through A, the multipart POST helper m (no rast), and the unrelated Vuex getter userid.

anchor.why: GET helper that, unless an override is provided, appends rast=(new Date).getTime().toString() to the URL and then calls o.a.get(t,...). This is where the observed rast query parameter is produced and attached.

roles.why: The loginmobile request function: i(t){var e="/sso/loginmobile";return Object(a["e"])(e,t)} routes the observed loginmobile GET through the rast-adding wrapper A (a["e"]). It carries the request to A but does not itself generate rast — a path/wrapper above the anchor.
Sibling /sso/login request function (o(t){..."/sso/login"...A}); routes a DIFFERENT endpoint through A. A near-identical lookalike decoy, not the observed loginmobile request.
Sibling /sso/loginmobilePwd request function; routes a different endpoint through A. A near-identical lookalike decoy.
Sibling /sso/logout request function; routes a different endpoint through A. A near-identical lookalike decoy.
A sibling multipart POST helper in the same http module. It issues a request but never adds rast; tempting but wrong.
An unrelated Vuex getter returning the user id; not on the request path.
